log.msg: THE FLEX F9-VS-D67 GAP, DIAGNOSED: taste/rate() scores whatever renders (proportions, spacing, alignment) and flex/ renders beautifully — confirmed by screenshot at 390/1280/3440, all clean. analyze()'s 75-point 'unreachable' rule checks something taste never asks: can a human actually SCROLL to it. Confirmed live with a real wheel event on the claimed tab: .pages.scrollTop stayed 0 on wheel (no scrollbar, no user-reachable scroll) while forcing scrollTop via JS moved content fine — exactly 'no scrollbar anywhere' as the rule defines it. The two tiers are not measuring the same page two ways; they are measuring two different things that happen to be almost fully decoupled on a rail+content layout.

ROOT CAUSE (one cause, all three pages, out of my fence): /web/layout/ calls this.catalog() (ext/catalog), which nests each child's real content inside .page-catalog-pages (catalog.css) — a region catalog.css never gives a bounded height or an overflow-y, because catalog.js's own decisions.md (2026-08-11) explicitly designed it around "the only scroller was the region", i.e. the OUTER app .pages was meant to do the scrolling. That assumption broke when styles.css picked up '.pages:not(:has(> .page.active-page)):not(:has(> .default)) { overflow-y: hidden }' (the 'only the region showing the leaf scrolls' rule, written for topic's nested-.pages pattern) — it also fires on the OUTER .pages whenever the active leaf is a catalog child, because the leaf lives inside .page-catalog-pages, not as a direct child of .pages. Net result: NOTHING in the ancestor chain scrolls. Verified live in a scratch iframe (no file touched): adding overflow-y:auto to .page-catalog-pages alone does nothing (confirmed clientHeight==scrollHeight, unbounded growth) because .page-catalog uses align-items:flex-start, so the region never receives a height ceiling to overflow against either — a real fix needs a Page.css '.fill'-style bounded+clipped box somewhere in the chain, not a one-line overflow tweak, and needs to be checked against the rail's position:sticky assumptions (catalog/doc/decisions.md).

BLAST RADIUS, not just my three pages: EVERY child of /web/layout/ trips it somewhere (flow F21, measure F19, grid F21@3440/C79@1280, tracks C77@3440) and EVERY child of /web/nav/ trips the identical selector-and-rule on div.page.flow.page-nav (sidebar F7, drawer F8, drill F18, rail C71@1280) — confirmed via findings.json, not guessed. This is a framework-wide catalog() defect, the same root cause the sibling agent fixing /web/nav/ this cycle is independently hitting. Recommend the mastermind treat it as ONE fix (styles.css + ext/catalog/catalog.css), not two separate page-level patches.

Every OTHER finding on the three pages also traces outside the public/web/layout/ fence or to an already-adjudicated decision, so ZERO in-fence edits were made: measure (~104-108 chars/line) is the site's own documented --measure:52em ceiling (layout-design skill: '52em is 83 to 103 characters... the token is the finding, not the page'); hit-size (60x17 range inputs) is ext/layout/layout.css's input.layout-range default; alignment (4-5px) is ext/demo's select.demo-zoom toolbar; pad-scale (26px vs 27px) is ext/highlight's pre.code-block — all three are shared framework chrome, not page-authored CSS. Two are TOOL FALSE POSITIVES with evidence: screens/'s 'whitespace' (93.5% of 589px empty) is probe.js's own documented IGNORE policy excluding .demo-screen from the model, mistaken by the whitespace rule for empty space — confirmed live, and probe.js's own comment already names this exact trade-off ('a page whose whole subject is a stage looks nearly empty'). respond/'s 'invisible' (ungrouped structure) undercounts Page.css's deliberately-bare page-preview-thumb cards as unpainted. Recorded for false-positives.md, not treated as a page defect.

Root cause, verified live without touching a file: ext/catalog's .page-catalog-pages has no bounded height or scroll context of its own (catalog's own decisions.md assumed the outer .pages would scroll it), and styles.css's newer '.pages:not(:has(active-page))... {overflow-y:hidden}' rule (written for the topic pattern) also silences that outer region whenever the active leaf is a catalog child — so nothing in the chain scrolls. Confirmed this is not page-specific: every /web/layout/ child (flow F21, measure F19, grid F21/C79, tracks C77) and every /web/nav/ child (sidebar F7, drawer F8, drill F18) trips the identical selector — one framework-wide catalog defect, same cause the sibling nav/ agent is independently hitting this cycle. The five secondary findings (measure/hit-size/alignment/pad-scale) all trace to shared framework chrome (ext/layout, ext/demo, ext/highlight) or the already-documented --measure:52em token; two more (screens/ whitespace, respond/ invisible) are confirmed tool false positives from probe.js's own documented demo-stage IGNORE policy and Page.css's deliberately-bare preview cards. Scores unchanged (flex F9/F9, screens F17/F19, respond F18/F19 at 1280/3440) because there was nothing safe or correct to change inside the fence — recommending the catalog+.pages scroll-chain fix to whoever owns framework/ext/catalog/catalog.css and public/styles.css.
